steps.title: Anchor sole plates and stand corner studs
steps.detail: Lay out the perimeter sole plates square on the subfloor deck and fasten the corner support studs plumb.

steps.title: Fasten wall top plates
steps.detail: Cap the corner support studs with 2x4 top plates around the perimeter, checking level across both axes.

steps.title: Erect ridge board and common rafters
steps.detail: Raise the 2x8 ridge board on temporary shores and nail the 2x6 common rafters at 9:12 pitch along the main roof.

steps.title: Install Dutch hip horizontal girder tie
steps.detail: Fasten the 2x8 horizontal girder tie across the common rafters at the Dutch hip break to carry the hip rafters and gablet wall.

steps.title: Frame mini-gablet wall above girder tie
steps.detail: Install the mini-gablet sole plate, center king stud, and flanking cripple studs up to the ridge board termination.

steps.title: Set 2x8 hip rafters and hip jack rafters
steps.detail: Fit the 2x8 hip rafters from the girder tie down to the corners, then install side and end jack rafters at 16-inch centers.

steps.title: Secure rafter connections with hurricane ties
steps.detail: Drive 1-1/2-inch framing nails through structural metal hurricane ties anchoring each common and hip rafter to the top plates.

entries.name: Exterior Insulation & Finish System (EIFS) Basecoat
entries.variant: 2 in EPS foam boards, 4.5 oz fiberglass mesh embedded in acrylic mortar
entries.material: Expanded polystyrene EPS board, polymer adhesive mortar, 4.5 oz woven fiberglass mesh, acrylic finish coat

tips.frame: Stagger EPS board joints horizontally in a running bond and rasp the entire foam face flat before basecoating.
general: Trowel basecoat adhesive directly onto EPS, then press fiberglass mesh into wet mortar from center outwards.
Overlap mesh edges by a minimum of 2-1/2 in and bridge 45-degree butterfly mesh strips across all window corners.

watchOut: Never leave mesh pattern visible or exposed dry; it must be fully encapsulated in the middle-to-outer third of the basecoat.
Do not align foam board seams with window or door jamb corners; route L-shaped cutout boards instead.

parts.name: Acrylic base coat mortar bed layer
Acrylic base coat embedding skim coat

steps.title: Frame the substrate wall section
steps.detail: Assemble the sole and top plates with four vertical studs spaced 400 mm on center, checking for squareness.

steps.title: Fasten sheathing and roll weather barrier
steps.detail: Screw the glass-mat gypsum sheathing to the framing and roll a continuous air/water-resistive membrane over the face.

steps.title: Trowel adhesive and hang EPS foam boards
steps.detail: Apply polymer adhesive with vertical notches and press 2-inch EPS boards with staggered running joints.

steps.title: Trowel base coat bed and embed fiberglass mesh
steps.detail: Apply a wet bed of polymer-modified base mortar and embed the 4.5 oz alkali-resistant mesh without wrinkles.

steps.title: Apply base coat skim and textured finish
steps.detail: Skim over the mesh to fully encapsulate the fiberglass, allow to cure, and float the acrylic textured finish coat.

entries.name: EMT Conduit Bending: 90° Stub, Saddle & Offset
entries.variant: 3/4 in EMT run with 90° bend, 3-bend saddle, box offset into 4S steel box
entries.material: 3/4 in EMT thinwall conduit, 4x4x2-1/8 in steel square box, 1-hole straps, steel set-screw connectors and couplings

tips.frame: Snap chalk lines marking obstruction center and box knockout locations on plywood board.
general: Deduct standard 6-inch take-up when calculating mark for 3/4 in EMT 90-degree stub-up bend.
Keep heavy foot pressure on the bender heel to eliminate conduit rippling and kink defects.

watchOut: Ream every conduit end thoroughly to prevent burrs from stripping wire insulation during pull.
Total degrees of bend between pull points must not exceed 360 degrees per NEC standards.

steps.title: Erect the training backboard
steps.detail: Fasten the vertical plywood backer board securely to the support cleats flush with the floor.

steps.title: Mount the junction box and crossing obstacle
steps.detail: Screw the 4S steel square box and the vertical obstacle conduit to the board layout marks.

steps.title: Bend and install the 90° stub-up
steps.detail: Bend a 90° stub on the hand bender using the arrow mark with a 6-inch deducer, then secure the riser with a 1-hole strap.

steps.title: Fabricate and position the 3-bend saddle
steps.detail: Execute a 45° center bend flanked by two 22.5° return bends to bridge the obstacle pipe cleanly without doglegs.

steps.title: Form the box offset and terminate into the 4S box
steps.detail: Kick a shallow 10° offset to align with the box knockout, assemble the coupling and box connector, and tighten all set screws.

entries.name: LVL Engineered Rim Board & Seismic Tie Connection
entries.variant: 1-1/4 in LVL rim board, treated 2x6 sill plate, Simpson LTP4 lateral ties
entries.material: 1-1/4 x 11-7/8 in LVL rim board, 2x6 treated mudsill, Simpson LTP4 framing angles, 10d x 1-1/2 in nails, 16d sinkers

tips.frame: Snap alignment lines along the outer edge of the sill plate to maintain a straight perimeter rim band for wall layout.
general: Toe-nail or clip engineered rim boards to the mudsill every 6 inches on center for code seismic shear transfer.
Stagger rim board end butt joints so they land over floor joist bearings or fall between joist centers per manufacturer code.

watchOut: Do not notch engineered LVL rim boards for deck ledgers or utility pipes without engineering evaluation.
Verify preservative-treated sill chemicals are compatible with metal tie plate coatings to avoid rapid corrosion.

steps.detail: Verify concrete stem wall elevation, squareness, and anchor bolt spacing before framing.

steps.title: Install sill gasket and bolt down mudsill
steps.detail: Lay capillary break sill gasket and drill the treated mudsill to fit anchor bolts, torquing 3-inch bearing plates securely.

steps.title: Erect and toe-nail LVL rim board
steps.detail: Align the 1-1/4 x 11-7/8 in LVL rim board flush with the exterior face of the mudsill and toe-nail with 16d sinkers.

steps.title: Frame floor I-joists to the rim board

steps.title: Fasten Simpson LTP4 seismic tie plates

entries.name: Resinous Epoxy Floor: Full Flake Broadcast & Clear Topcoat
entries.variant: 100% solids epoxy base, 1/4 in vinyl chips full-refusal, UV topcoat
entries.material: 2-part 100% solids epoxy basecoat, decorative PVA color flakes, 2-part polyaspartic clear topcoat, spiked shoes

tips.frame: Diamond-grind the concrete slab to an open Concrete Surface Profile CSP-2/3 and vacuum all residual dust.
general: Spread mixed epoxy basecoat with a notched squeegee and back-roll with a 3/8 in lint-free roller for uniform mil thickness.
Broadcast vinyl color flakes upwards into the air by handfuls, throwing to complete saturation ('rejection') while wearing spiked shoes.

watchOut: Respect batch pot-life strictly (typically 20-30 minutes); massed mixed epoxy generates rapid exothermic heat and hardens in the pail.
Scrape and vacuum all unbonded loose flakes flat before applying the clear polyaspartic protective topcoat.

parts.name: 100 percent solids pigmented epoxy floor basecoat
100 percent solids epoxy vertical cove primer coat
Polyaspartic clear lock and seal coat

steps.title: Set concrete substrate and fill control joints
steps.detail: Diamond grind concrete substrate to ICRI CSP-2 profile and inject semi-rigid polyurea joint filler flush with slab surface.

steps.title: Install perimeter stops and cove base cant
steps.detail: Anchor aluminum termination profiles at floor perimeters and trowel 45-degree epoxy mortar cove cant against the backer curb.

steps.title: Mix and squeegee 100 percent solids epoxy basecoat
steps.detail: Spread pigmented epoxy receiving coat across slab at 12 to 16 mils using a notched squeegee and brush-coat vertical cove face.

steps.title: Broadcast color flakes to full refusal with spiked shoes
steps.detail: Walk onto the wet epoxy using spiked shoes and cast 1/4-inch vinyl chips upward to rejection until floor surface is completely saturated.

steps.title: Scrape excess flakes and apply clear polyaspartic lock coat
steps.detail: Scrape standing chip edges flat with a floor scraper, vacuum loose flake refusal, and squeegee-apply clear polyaspartic lock coat.

steps.title: Roll final UV clear polyaspartic wear coat
steps.detail: Cross-roll the final aliphatic polyaspartic clear topcoat evenly to create a chemical-resistant, UV-stable high-traffic wear surface.

entries.name: Epoxy Terrazzo Floor: Zinc Divider Strips & Marble Aggregate
entries.variant: 3/8 in matrix bed, 1/4 in zinc L-strips, #1/#2 marble chips, epoxy primer
entries.material: Zinc L-angle divider strips, moisture-tolerant epoxy primer, colored epoxy matrix resin, crushed marble chips

tips.frame: Set zinc divider strips onto chalk lines using fast-setting epoxy adhesive, checking exact strip height with a straightedge.
general: Mix marble aggregate with pigmented epoxy resin at a 5:1 weight ratio until completely wetted out.
Trowel matrix between divider strips slightly proud (1/16 in), pack with a hand roller, and cure before rotary wet-grinding.

watchOut: Concrete substrate vapor emissions exceeding 3 lbs/1000 sq ft/24 hr require a dedicated epoxy vapor-suppression primer.
Rotary grinding generates heavy slurry; maintain slurry collection vacuums and wear respiratory protection.

steps.title: Inspect concrete substrate
steps.detail: Verify the concrete slab is shot-blasted to CSP-3 profile, dry, and clean of laitance.

steps.title: Apply moisture-mitigating primer
steps.detail: Roll 100% solids epoxy primer uniformly across the prepared slab surface to prevent pinholing.

steps.title: Set perimeter zinc divider strips
steps.detail: Bed 1/4 in zinc L-angle strips along the perimeter edges into structural epoxy adhesive, checking alignment.

steps.title: Install field divider grid
steps.detail: Set interior zinc divider strips to divide the field into equal quadrants, ensuring flush joints at strip intersections.

steps.title: Pour and screed epoxy terrazzo matrix
steps.detail: Trowel blended pigmented epoxy resin and #1/#2 marble aggregate to 3/8 in depth flush with zinc tops.

entries.name: Fiber Cement Lap Siding: Blind-Nailed with Joint Flashing
entries.variant: 5/16 x 8-1/4 in planks, 7 in exposure, composite trim, 0.019 in joint tabs
entries.material: Fiber cement lap siding, prefinished corner trim, 0.019 in aluminum joint flashing, 2 in HDG ring-shank coil nails

tips.frame: Install a level 1/4 in fiber cement starter strip at the wall base to kick out the initial lap course.
general: Center 3 in wide aluminum flashing slips behind all factory butt joints without caulking the vertical seam.
Blind-nail 1 in down from the top edge directly into wall studs at 16 in O.C.

watchOut: Crystalline silica dust hazard: use dedicated dust-collecting shears or diamond fiber-cement circular saw blades with HEPA vacuums.
Never over-drive nails; fastener heads must sit flush with the board face without breaking the cement core.

steps.title: Frame wall mockup structure
steps.detail: Lay out sole and top plates with studs spaced at 16 inches on center, nailing through plates into stud ends with two 16d nails per connection.

steps.title: Fasten sheathing and moisture barrier
steps.detail: Fasten OSB sheathing flush across the frame, then install water-resistive barrier flat with seams lapped shedding water downward.

steps.title: Install corner trims and starter strip
steps.detail: Plumb prefinished corner trim boards on both sides and nail the continuous fiber cement starter strip level along the base plate.

steps.title: Position joint tab and blind-nail course one
steps.detail: Center a 0.019-inch aluminum joint flashing tab behind the center butt joint, maintaining a moderate butt gap, and blind-nail planks 1 inch below top edge into studs.

steps.title: Install courses two and three with staggered joints
steps.detail: Snap chalk lines at 7-inch exposure, slide flashing behind butt joints over framing studs, and blind-nail through overlapping laps into each stud.

steps.title: Run courses four and five maintaining joint offset
steps.detail: Continue stepping joints across alternate stud bays, keeping 1/8-inch expansion clearance to corner trims and ensuring nails penetrate at least 1-1/4 inches into solid framing.

entries.name: Millworker: Fireplace Mantel & Pilaster Surround Assembly
entries.variant: Fluted poplar pilasters, plinth blocks, frieze panel, layered crown mantel shelf, non-combustible clearances
entries.material: Poplar S4S lumber, plinth blocks, fluted casing, 3/4 in birch ply mantel core, crown molding, pocket screws

tips.frame: Confirm firebox non-combustible perimeter margins according to NFPA 211 before sizing surround components.
general: Pre-assemble pilasters, plinth blocks, and the frieze breast panel into a rigid face assembly on workbench benches before mounting.
Mount a heavy wood French cleat to wall studs, then drop the hollow box mantel shelf over it and blind-nail from above.

watchOut: NFPA 211 mandates a minimum 6 in clearance between combustible wood trim and the fireplace firebox opening.
Any combustible mantel projection exceeding 1-1/2 in thickness requires at least 12 in clearance above the firebox opening.

steps.title: Fasten wall return jambs and frieze backer
steps.detail: Plumb and secure the outer wall returns, firebox reveal jambs, and plywood frieze ground to wall framing maintaining required clearances.

steps.title: Set base plinth blocks and capital blocks
steps.detail: Bed plinth blocks flush to finished floor and level the capital blocks above the pilaster line using finish screws.

steps.title: Install pilaster ground stiles and fluted casings
steps.detail: Fasten the poplar backing stiles between returns, then center and pin the fluted pilaster casings tightly between plinths and capitals.

steps.title: Mount frieze breast board and decorative tablet
steps.detail: Fasten the solid poplar frieze face over the structural plywood backer and center the decorative applique tablet.

steps.title: Fit crown backer, cove crown, and bed plate
steps.detail: Fasten the continuous crown backing block, apply the profiled crown molding with mitered returns, and set the bed plate on top.

steps.title: Cap mantel shelf assembly
steps.detail: Anchor the birch plywood core shelf down through the bed plate and face-glue and secure the layered solid poplar mantel cap.

entries.name: Flush LVL Floor Girder with Concealed Hangers
entries.variant: Triple 1-3/4 x 11-7/8 in LVL beam, Simpson HUC concealed flange hangers, 2x10 floor joists
entries.material: 1-3/4 x 11-7/8 in laminated veneer lumber (LVL), 2x10 SPF joists, Simpson HUC210 concealed hangers, structural screws, framing nails

tips.frame: Laminate the 3-ply LVL girder on sawhorses using staggered two-row patterns of 3 in structural screws.
general: Snap hanger height lines on the LVL face allowing 1/8 in joist crown projection above the beam for flush subfloor plane.
Nail concealed hanger side flanges tight to the girder before dropping joist ends into position.

watchOut: Never install drywall screws or non-rated fasteners into engineered structural joist hangers.
Seat joists tight to the back and bottom of the hanger seat; maximum permissible gap is 1/8 in.

steps.title: Laminate the Triple LVL Girder
steps.detail: Align the three 1-3/4 in x 11-7/8 in LVL plies edge-to-edge and face-to-face. Clamp tightly together and drive structural lamination screws in a staggered pattern across both faces.

steps.title: Layout and Fasten Concealed Joist Hangers
steps.detail: Mark joist stations at 16 in (400 mm) on-center along the front and rear faces of the beam. Fasten Simpson HUC210 concealed flange hangers through the inward-turned header flanges with structural screws.

steps.title: Drop Floor Joists into Concealed Pockets
steps.detail: Slide 2x10 floor joists into each hanger seat so the tops finish exactly flush with the top edge of the LVL girder. Fasten joist sides through the hanger prong holes.

steps.title: Install End Headers and Outer Rim Joists
steps.detail: Position the outer rim joists and side boundary headers against the joist ends. Check assembly diagonals for square and secure with 16d framing nails driven through the rim into each joist butt.

entries.name: Gambrel Rafter Truss with Plywood Gussets
entries.variant: 2x6 lower steep rafter, 2x6 upper shallow rafter, 1/2 in plywood gussets, horizontal collar tie
entries.material: SPF 2x6 rafters, 1/2 in CDX plywood gusset plates, 1x6 collar ties, 8d common nails, wood glue

tips.frame: Build a wooden layout jig on the subfloor to repeat identical rafter angles and gusset placements.
general: Apply structural wood glue generously between rafter meeting joints and gusset faces before nailing.
Fasten gusset plates on both sides using a uniform row-and-column nail pattern as specified by engineering.

watchOut: Ensure the pitch transition knuckles on opposing sides of the building line up with tight string lines.
Never stand an unbraced gambrel rafter pair without immediate diagonal ground bracing.

steps.title: Lay out lower and upper rafters on assembly jig
steps.detail: Position the steep 2x6 lower rafters and shallow 2x6 upper rafters flat on layout stops, ensuring plumb cuts butt tightly at the ridge and knuckle transitions.

steps.title: Fasten back collar tie and back gusset plates
steps.detail: Apply construction adhesive beneath joints and nail the back 1x6 collar tie along with the peak, knuckle, and heel plywood gusset plates using 8d common nails.

steps.title: Install front collar tie
steps.detail: Span the front 1x6 collar tie across both knuckle joints, checking horizontal alignment with a spirit level before nailing off into rafter faces.

steps.title: Secure front peak, knuckle, and heel gussets
steps.detail: Glue and fasten front CDX plywood gussets over the peak, knuckles, and heels with staggered 8d nail patterns spaced 75 mm on center.

entries.name: Gambrel Mansard Roof Pitch-Break Plywood Gusset
entries.variant: 6:12 upper rafter to 18:12 lower rafter, dual 1/2 in CDX plywood gussets
entries.material: 2x6 SPF lumber, 1/2 in CDX structural plywood gusset plates, polyurethane subfloor adhesive, 8d ring-shank nails

tips.frame: Build a floor jig with wooden stop blocks to repeatably fit upper and lower rafter angles together before gusset attachment.
general: Apply generous adhesive between lumber and plywood gussets before pneumatic nailing on both faces.
Ensure lower steep rafter birdsmouth cut seats level over the perimeter wall double top plate.

watchOut: Gusset nails must not penetrate through the opposite face and become exposed shiners without clinching.
Wear eye protection when air-nailing into plywood gussets prone to wood splinters.

steps.title: Lay out and align pitch-break framing
steps.detail: Fit the 18:12 lower curb rafter, 6:12 upper rafter, and horizontal curb tie tight at the knuckle junction.

steps.title: Glue and fasten front CDX gusset
steps.detail: Apply polyurethane subfloor adhesive across the joint face and drive 29 8d ring-shank nails into the framing members.

steps.title: Glue and fasten rear CDX gusset
steps.detail: Roll the assembly over, apply polyurethane adhesive, and nail the opposing gusset plate with 29 8d ring-shank nails.

entries.name: Narrow Garage Wall Portal Frame with Tension Straps
entries.variant: Double 2x4 jambs, continuous structural sheathing, CS16 steel tension straps
entries.material: Double 2x4 framing, 1/2 in APA rated structural plywood, Simpson CS16 coil strap, 5/8 in anchor bolts, 8d nails

tips.frame: Plumb portal frame leg studs carefully before spanning the engineered header across the opening.
general: Wrap continuous tension strapping tightly around header-to-jamb junctions according to manufacturer nail patterns.
Nail plywood sheathing with tight 3-inch perimeter spacing into both the header and pony leg members.

watchOut: Ensure anchor bolts have minimum 7-inch embedment with heavy bearing washers to avoid blowout under seismic uplift.
Do not substitute undersized nails into portal framing straps; shear load relies strictly on full-shank fasteners.

Anchor bolt left inner with washer

Anchor bolt right outer with washer

Continuous header APA rated structural plywood

steps.title: Set foundation curb and anchor bolts
steps.detail: Cast the foundation slab curb and embed 5/8 in anchor bolts with plate washers at each portal frame pier location.

steps.title: Fasten treated sole plates
steps.detail: Drill clearance holes in the treated 2x4 sole plates and torque down nuts onto 3x3 in heavy plate washers.

steps.title: Frame double jambs and wall studs
steps.detail: Plumb and toe-nail the outer studs, intermediate studs, and double jamb stud assemblies onto each portal pier sole plate.

steps.title: Install continuous portal header and top plates
steps.detail: Position the built-up double 2x4 header across the portal opening spanning onto both piers, then cap with double top plates.

steps.title: Fasten CS16 steel tension straps
steps.detail: Fasten Simpson CS16 coil straps vertically across the portal header down onto the double jamb studs to resist overturning moment.

steps.title: Fasten APA rated structural sheathing
steps.detail: Nail 1/2 in APA rated plywood sheathing continuously over the portal piers and across the header at code-specified perimeter spacing.

entries.name: Natural Gas Black Iron Header & Sediment Trap
entries.variant: 1 in Sch 40 black pipe supply, 1/2 in drop, sediment trap and union
entries.material: Sch 40 black steel pipe, malleable iron threaded fittings, brass gas ball valve, gas-rated PTFE tape

tips.frame: Secure main vertical header using split-ring pipe hangers on 3/8 in threaded rod.
general: Construct sediment trap (dirt leg) downstream of shutoff valve with minimum 3-inch nipple pocket.
Apply thread sealant to male threads only, leaving first two threads bare to prevent valve clogging.

watchOut: Never install gas union downstream of appliance shutoff without ground-joint face alignment.
Test piping at minimum 1.5 times operating pressure (or 3 PSI gauge) with certified gauge block.

parts.name: 1 in x 1 in x 1/2 in reducing tee
1/2 in x 4 in sediment trap nipple

steps.title: Mount backer panel and strut framing
steps.detail: Fasten the backer panel plumb and level, then attach the upper and lower Unistrut mounting rails across the board.

steps.title: Assemble and secure 1 in supply header
steps.detail: Apply gas-rated PTFE tape and pipe dope to 1 in male threads, make up the reducing tee and extension cap, then bolt the supply clamp to the upper strut.

steps.title: Install upper drop and gas ball valve
steps.detail: Thread the 1/2 in close nipple into the reducing tee branch, install the shutoff valve with handle facing front, and thread in the vertical drop riser.

steps.title: Construct sediment trap drip pocket
steps.detail: Thread the tee straight onto the vertical drop, then install the minimum 3 in sediment nipple into the bottom outlet and tighten the iron cap.

steps.title: Make up appliance union and secure line
steps.detail: Extend the branch through the connecting nipple, assemble the ground-joint union metal-to-metal, and clamp the discharge run to the lower strut channel.

entries.name: Octagonal Roof Rafters & Center Compression Hub
entries.variant: Heavy 1/4 in welded steel compression ring, eight 2x6 hip rafters at 6:12 pitch, rim fascia
entries.material: Structural steel octagonal hub plate, SPF 2x6 rafters, 1/2 in through-bolts, exterior timber screws, 2x8 fascia

tips.frame: Support the center steel compression ring on a temporary adjustable center prop post set to the exact ridge height.
general: Install opposing pairs of 2x6 hip rafters sequentially to balance lateral thrust against the center ring.
Miter birdsmouth cuts precisely to maintain full bearing across the octagonal perimeter plate angles.

watchOut: Do not remove the temporary center shoring post until all eight hip rafters and perimeter fascia boards are secured.
Check bolt alignment through steel tabs before driving bolts to prevent cross-threading or wood splitting.

steps.title: Erect temporary center shoring tower
steps.detail: Lay the mudsill plate flat on floor center and plumb the 6x6 shoring post beneath the bolster cap to support the hub height.

steps.title: Seat the welded compression ring
steps.detail: Set the octagonal steel compression ring centered on the shoring bolster with shear tabs oriented along the 45-degree layout axes.

steps.title: Hang opposing cardinal rafters
steps.detail: Raise opposing East-West and North-South hip rafters into their hub tab slots and through-bolt each end with 1/2 in steel hardware.

steps.title: Install corner hip rafters
steps.detail: Hoist the four intermediate diagonal hip rafters at 6:12 pitch into the remaining hub shear plates and torque through-bolts snugly.

steps.title: Fasten perimeter rim fascia segments
steps.detail: Wrap the perimeter tails with 2x8 sub-fascia boards mitered at 22.5 degrees, screwing each segment into the plumb-cut rafter plumb ends.

entries.name: Glulam Beam Pocket in Concrete Foundation
entries.variant: 5-1/8 x 15 in glulam girder, 1/2 in air space, neoprene bearing pad, embedded steel tie strap
entries.material: 24F-V4 architectural glulam beam, 60-durometer neoprene pad, 12-ga galvanized tie strap, expansion concrete anchors

tips.frame: Lay out the beam seat level at exact finished floor minus girder depth minus bearing pad thickness.
general: Maintain a minimum 1/2 in clearance on all wood faces from direct concrete contact to prevent rot.
Seal end grain of the glulam with paraffin wax or approved water-resistant barrier before insertion.

watchOut: Do not encase the top or ends of the glulam in wet grout or mortar; timber needs expansion space to breathe.
Verify minimum required bearing length (typically 3-1/2 inches) on the concrete ledge.

steps.title: Cast Foundation Wall with Beam Pocket
steps.detail: Form and place concrete foundation wall with an integrated pocket providing 160 mm width and 200 mm depth, ensuring level bearing seat.

steps.title: Set Neoprene Bearing Pad
steps.detail: Center the 60-durometer neoprene pad on the pocket floor to isolate the timber beam from concrete moisture migration.

steps.title: Fly and Position Glulam Girder
steps.detail: Lower the 5-1/8 x 15 inch glulam beam onto the neoprene pad, maintaining 1/2-inch air space at both sides and the beam end.

steps.title: Fasten Tie Strap and Anchors
steps.detail: Secure the 12-gauge angle strap to the concrete cheek using expansion anchors, then drive heavy timber screws into the girder flank.

entries.name: Heavy Timber Glulam Girder & Flush Purlin Joint
entries.variant: 6-3/4 x 24 in glulam girder, 4x8 solid purlins, aluminum dovetail concealed connectors (Knapp/Ricon)
entries.material: Architectural grade 24F glulam beam, 4x8 Douglas fir purlins, machined aluminum dovetail plates, specialized Torx timber screws

tips.frame: Route mortise pockets into purlin ends using manufacturer jigs to ensure connectors sit completely flush.
general: Mount female receiving plates onto the main glulam girder using precision layout templates and guide pins.
Drop purlins into position vertically until the interlocking dovetail wedge engages with an audible click.

watchOut: Ensure all connector screws are driven dead perpendicular; angled screw heads prevent dovetails from dropping flush.
Check that router mortise depth matches connector thickness exactly to maintain structural fire-resistance ratings.

steps.title: Set primary glulam girder
steps.desc: Position the 6-3/4 x 24 architectural glulam girder on stable timber cribbing and verify level alignment.

steps.title: Mortise and secure female receiver plates
steps.desc: Rout 12 mm deep mortises into the girder flanks flush with connector depth, then drive specialized Torx wood screws through the aluminum dovetail female plates.

steps.title: Attach male insert plates to purlins
steps.desc: Mortise and fasten the companion aluminum dovetail male insert plates to the end grain of each 4x8 purlin using high-strength structural screws.

steps.title: Slide purlins into concealed dovetail receivers
steps.desc: Lower purlins vertically into the female housings until their top faces align dead flush with the top of the glulam girder.

steps.title: Drive anti-uplift safety locking pins
steps.desc: Drive steel retaining pins through the pre-drilled access holes to wedge the dovetail connection securely against seismic and wind uplift forces.

entries.name: Green Roof Drain Inspection Chamber & Ballast Stop
entries.variant: 12x12 in perforated stainless steel chamber, removable locking lid, 4 in aluminum gravel stop edge trim
entries.material: 16-ga perforated 304 stainless box, slotted aluminum edge trim, drainage retention cup mat, river rock ballast

tips.frame: Center the stainless chamber directly above the primary roof drain basin without puncturing the waterproofing slip sheet.
general: Surround the chamber perimeter with a 12-inch wide border of rounded washed drainage ballast rock.
Fasten slotted gravel stops to drainage matting to keep growth media separated from clear rock drainage zones.

watchOut: Keep fine engineered planting soil from entering the inspection chamber; fines will quickly plug roof drains.
Never fasten gravel stops or inspection wells with mechanical screws into or through the underlying roof membrane.

parts.name: Cast iron roof drain bowl and clamping collar
Dimpled water retention and drainage cup mat
12x12 in perforated stainless steel inspection chamber
Washed river rock drain ballast apron
Extensive green roof growing medium and sedum
Stainless steel removable locking inspection lid

steps.title: Set structural deck and primary drain sump
steps.detail: Verify substrate level and bolt down the primary roof drain clamping ring centered over the roof penetration.

steps.title: Roll out drainage cups and separation fleece
steps.detail: Install the dimpled retention cup mat flush around the drain collar and overlay with needle-punched filter fleece.

steps.title: Assemble slotted aluminum gravel stop collar
steps.detail: Position the four 4-inch slotted gravel stop trims in a square perimeter collar to isolate the drain ballast zone.

steps.title: Seat perforated stainless inspection chamber
steps.detail: Set the 12x12 inch perforated stainless steel inspection chamber centered over the drain outlet on the fleece.

steps.title: Place river rock ballast and growing medium
steps.detail: Fill the inner apron with washed river rock ballast and spread engineered green roof growing medium outside the trim.

steps.title: Install and lock inspection chamber lid
steps.detail: Seat the stainless steel locking lid over the chamber rim and engage the quarter-turn security latch.

entries.name: Extensive Green Roof Modular Drainage Tray
entries.variant: Pre-planted 4 in depth interlocking poly trays with root barrier slip sheet
entries.material: Polypropylene modular trays, engineered mineral substrate, sedum plugs, 30-mil root barrier, drain fabric

tips.frame: Sweep the roofing membrane clean and lay continuous protective root barrier before placing trays.
general: Engage tray side-locking lugs securely to prevent lateral drift under heavy wind uplift.
Maintain a clean, gravel ballast boundary 12 inches away from roof drains and perimeter flashing.

watchOut: Verify structural deck live-load capacity accounts for fully saturated soil and plant mass.

steps.title: Lay Root Barrier Slip Sheet
steps.desc: Unroll the 30-mil polyethylene root barrier sheet over the roof waterproofing assembly, ensuring smooth placement free of wrinkles or punctures.

steps.title: Place Interlocking Polypropylene Trays
steps.desc: Position the 4-inch deep polypropylene drainage trays directly on the root barrier, snapping adjacent perimeter tongue-and-groove tabs firmly together.

steps.title: Install Aluminum Perimeter Edge Restraints
steps.desc: Butt the perforated L-shaped aluminum edge angles tightly against the outer tray rims to contain the modular layout and maintain free drainage pathways.

steps.title: Fit Drainage Filter Fabric Liners
steps.desc: Lay the non-woven geotextile fabric inserts flat across the bottom of each tray over the water retention cups to prevent aggregate migration.

steps.title: Deposit Engineered Mineral Substrate
steps.desc: Evenly distribute the engineered extensive growing medium to a depth of 60 mm, screeding the lightweight expanded mineral aggregate flush.

steps.title: Install Sedum Vegetative Mats
steps.desc: Place the pre-cultivated sedum vegetative tiles over the substrate layer, butting seams tightly together and tamping lightly to establish root contact.

entries.name: Hardwood Flooring: Blind-Nailed Tongue & Groove
entries.variant: 3/4 x 3-1/4 in solid red oak, 15 lb asphalt felt, 2 in cleats at 8 in O.C.
entries.material: Solid red oak T&G boards, 15 lb roofing felt, 2 in L-cleats, 1-1/2 in finish nails

tips.frame: Snap a primary chalk line parallel to the longest unobstructed wall offset by the board width plus a 3/4 in expansion gap.
general: Rack out 4 to 5 bundles ahead to mix grain patterns and stagger end-joints by at least 6 in.
Blind-nail through the tongue at a 45-degree angle using a pneumatic floor nailer with rubber mallet.

watchOut: Acclimate solid wood flooring on-site until moisture content is within 2-4% of the subfloor before fastening.
Never crowd perimeter walls; maintain a 3/4 in gap to prevent buckled flooring during seasonal humidity spikes.

steps.title: Secure the plywood subfloor panels
steps.detail: Lay the 3/4 in OSB subfloor panels tight over the framing and fasten with structural subfloor screws at 12 in on-centre.

steps.title: Roll out 15 lb asphalt saturated felt
steps.detail: Install vapor retarder felt across the subfloor with a 4 in overlap at seams, tacking with staple nails to prevent shifting.

steps.title: Set and align the starter courses
steps.detail: Establish the 3/4 in perimeter expansion gap, face-nail the starter edge, and blind-nail through the tongue pocket at a 45 degree angle.

steps.title: Blind-nail field courses with L-cleats
steps.detail: Engage tongue-and-groove joints tightly with a flooring mallet and seat 2 in cleats at 8 in intervals along each board.

steps.title: Install and face-nail finishing rows
steps.detail: Lever the final courses snugly into position with a pry bar, blind-nailing where space permits and face-nailing the final border.

entries.name: Trim Carpenter: Hardwood Stair Tread & Riser Fitment
entries.variant: 1-1/16 in red oak bullnose treads, 3/4 in poplar risers, stair tread template jig
entries.material: Red oak tread blanks, primed poplar risers, polyurethane construction adhesive, 15-ga finish nails

tips.frame: Establish identical riser heights from finished bottom landing to finished upper landing.
general: Transfer stringer angles and tread lengths simultaneously using an adjustable mechanical stair tread template tool.
Apply heavy beads of elastomeric polyurethane adhesive to stringers to prevent seasonal squeaking.

watchOut: IRC limits tread-to-tread riser height variation to a maximum of 3/8 in across the complete flight.
Tread nosing overhang must measure uniformly between 3/4 in and 1-1/4 in beyond the riser below.

steps.title: Erect stringer carriages and side skirtboards
steps.detail: Secure the three rough-cut carriages to the floor cleats and upper header, then plumb and nail both primed skirtboards.

steps.title: Install bottom poplar riser
steps.detail: Apply construction adhesive beads to the first riser cut and nail the 3/4-inch poplar riser tight between skirtboards.

steps.title: Bed and fasten red oak Tread 1
steps.detail: Lay polyurethane adhesive across the stringer run and bed the 1-1/16-inch red oak tread, aligning a uniform 1-1/4-inch bullnose overhang.

steps.title: Template, scribe, and fit Step 2 riser and tread
steps.detail: Lock the stair template jig firmly against both skirtboards to scribe the exact angles and lengths, then glue and nail Riser 2 and Tread 2.

steps.title: Fit and bed Riser 3 and Tread 3
steps.detail: Transfer jig dimensions to the third set of blanks, apply continuous urethane adhesive beads, and set the tread with blind heel nails.

steps.title: Close assembly with top landing riser
steps.detail: Scribe and pin Riser 4 against the upper landing header to complete the closed-stringer hardwood stair trim.

entries.name: HRV Core Installation & Balancing Ductwork
entries.variant: 150 CFM residential HRV, 6 in insulated flex intake/exhaust, rigid metal branch
entries.material: HRV cabinet, 6 in R-6 insulated flex duct, 6 in galvanized sheet metal duct, balancing dampers, Magnehelic test ports

tips.frame: Suspend unit from ceiling framing using vibration isolation springs and rubber bushings.
general: Seal inner duct vapor core with mastic and foil tape, then pull insulation blanket outer jacket tight.
Drill pressure tap ports 2.5 duct diameters upstream from balancing dampers for accurate airflow reads.

watchOut: Condensate lines must drop into a dedicated trap with at least 2 inches of water seal to avoid backdraft.
Keep fresh air intake hood separated by minimum 10 feet from dryer, furnace, or gas exhaust terminations.

steps.title: Erect studs and backer panel
steps.detail: Anchor framing studs at 500 mm centers and fasten the 3/4-inch plywood backer panel flush to the framing face.

steps.title: Mount suspension rail and hang cabinet
steps.detail: Level and secure the suspension bracket to the backer board, then hang the HRV cabinet into the interlocking flange.

steps.title: Install duct collars and P-trap drain
steps.detail: Attach 6-inch starting collars to all four air ports with sheet metal screws and connect the condensate P-trap at the base drain.

steps.title: Fasten insulated intake and exhaust flex
steps.detail: Slide R-6 insulated flexible ducts over the outdoor collars, seal the inner liner with mastic, and cinch tight with gear clamps.

steps.title: Fit rigid branch ducts and balancing dampers
steps.detail: Slip galvanized rigid duct sleeves over the indoor collars and secure inline quadrant balancing dampers into both supply and return lines.

steps.title: Mount test ports and manometer for balancing
steps.detail: Thread differential pressure test ports into each duct stream and connect sensing tubes to the Magnehelic gauge to balance CFM across the core.

entries.name: Asphalt Pavement Longitudinal Joint Compaction
entries.variant: 2 in wearing course lift, vertical joint butt face, PG 64-22 tack coat, matched rolling passes
entries.material: Hot-mix asphalt 9.5 mm surface mix, emulsified asphalt tack coat (SS-1h), joint adhesive rubber tape

tips.frame: Trim the cold lane edge with a clean vertical pavement saw cut or milling wheel before placing adjacent hot lane.
general: Paint vertical cold face heavily with uniform tack coat or rubberized joint adhesive to bond and seal the seam.
Overlap hot fresh mat over cold lane by 1 to 1.5 inches, luting excess material back onto the hot side with an asphalt rake.

watchOut: Roll first pass with steel tandem drum roller riding primarily on cold lane, overlapping hot mat by only 6 inches to pinch joint tightly.
Never scatter coarse rake-off aggregate across the finished hot mat, which creates surface voids and early raveling.

steps.title: Prepare binder course and spray tack coat
steps.detail: Clean the underlying binder course and apply emulsified asphalt tack coat uniformly across the lift area to ensure interlayer shear bonding.

steps.title: Place and trim cold lane butt joint
steps.detail: Lay and compact the cold pass wearing course, then cut back unconfined edges with a wheel cutter to expose a sound vertical aggregate face.

steps.title: Apply vertical joint adhesive tape
steps.detail: Adhere polymer-modified joint tape firmly along the vertical face of the cold mat to prevent moisture intrusion and edge crumbling.

steps.title: Pave hot lane with joint overlap surcharge
steps.detail: Screed the hot surface mix with a 25 mm overlap onto the cold lane and maintain loose surcharge thickness for matched roller consolidation.

steps.title: Verify joint compaction and transverse planarity
steps.detail: Perform matched tandem roller passes pinching the joint line, then inspect cross-joint smoothness using the straightedge and tolerance wedge.

entries.name: Commercial Kitchen Grease Interceptor Assembly
entries.variant: 50 GPM hydromechanical grease trap, vented flow control tee, and cleanouts
entries.material: Polyethylene commercial grease interceptor, PVC flow control fitting, Schedule 40 DWV piping, air-relief vent

tips.frame: Set unit on a level concrete pad with clearance around lid latches for kitchen service access.
general: Install the calibrated vented flow control fitting upstream of the inlet to maintain separation velocity.
Connect the air-relief vent from the flow control fitting directly back into the building vent stack.

watchOut: Operating an interceptor without the certified flow control fitting causes wash-through and sewer line clogs.

steps.title: Set and Anchor Grease Interceptor Tank
steps.desc: Place the hydromechanical interceptor tank flat on the slab, check level in both directions, and fasten the four base flange brackets with floor anchors. Verify internal flow diffuser and retention baffles are seated securely in their molded tracks.

steps.title: Install Inlet Flow Control Fitting and Air-Relief Vent
steps.desc: Couple the calibrated 50 GPM flow control fitting to the inlet spigot with the internal orifice facing upstream. Solvent-weld the vertical air-relief vent riser and install the directional inlet cleanout tee with its threaded inspection plug.

steps.title: Complete Cleanouts and Discharge Drain Connections
steps.desc: Connect the outlet adapter spigot to the discharge cleanout tee, verifying a 1/4 inch per foot downward drainage slope toward the waste tailpiece. Seat the threaded brass cleanout plug with Teflon tape.

steps.title: Fit Gasketed Access Cover and Hold-Down Hardware
steps.desc: Position the continuous neoprene odor gasket along the tank rim and seat the heavy-duty polyethylene cover. Secure the left and right structural hold-down crossbars using the perimeter bolt assemblies to maintain an air- and water-tight seal.

entries.name: Hydronic Radiant Heating Manifold & PEX Loops
entries.variant: 4-loop stainless supply/return manifold, flow meters, 1/2 in barrier PEX
entries.material: Stainless steel manifold, 1/2 in EVOH PEX, brass ball valves, euroconus compression fittings, unistrut

tips.frame: Anchor unistrut backing tracks level at 30 inches above finished floor.
general: Cut PEX tubing square and deburr before seating fully against the Euroconus shoulder.
Maintain a minimum 5-inch bend radius without kinking by using preformed plastic bend supports.

watchOut: Always maintain 50 PSI pneumatic test pressure while pouring slab or closing walls.
Use oxygen-barrier PEX only; non-barrier tubing will corrode cast-iron circulators.

Supply air vent and drain/fill valve
Return isolation ball valve with blue thermometer
Return air vent and drain/fill valve
1/2 in red EVOH barrier PEX supply drops
1/2 in blue EVOH barrier PEX return drops

steps.title: Mount backer board and unistrut channels
steps.detail: Fasten 3/4-in plywood backer board plumb and level to wall studs. Anchor upper and lower unistrut mounting channels at 850 mm and 640 mm elevations.

steps.title: Attach manifold mounting brackets
steps.detail: Secure the stepped manifold brackets to both strut channels with spring channel nuts, setting the lower cradle forward to clear supply loop drops.

steps.title: Mount supply and return manifold headers
steps.detail: Seat the 1-1/4 in stainless supply header in the top rear clamp and the return header in the bottom front clamp, tightening rubber-isolated clamp bands.

steps.title: Install flow meters and balancing valves
steps.detail: Thread the four visual flow meter sight glasses into top supply ports and four balancing shutoff valves onto lower return ports.

steps.title: Install ball valves and purge assemblies
steps.detail: Thread 1-in main isolation valves with integrated dial thermometers onto the supply and return inlets, and install combined air vent/drain assemblies on the opposite ends.

steps.title: Connect euroconus adapters and PEX drops
steps.detail: Mount euroconus compression adapters to all 8 branch outlets. Cut 1/2-in oxygen barrier PEX squarely and torque compression nuts to manufacturer spec.

steps.title: Snap bend supports at floor transition
steps.detail: Snap heavy-duty 90-degree metal bend supports onto each PEX drop at slab entry to protect tubes from kinking and mechanical abrasion.

entries.name: Knee-Braced Post-and-Beam Porch Bent
entries.variant: 6x6 cedar posts, 6x10 beam, 4x4 braces with 45-degree timber screw joints
entries.material: Rough-sawn western red cedar 6x6 posts, 6x10 header, 4x4 diagonal knee braces, 8 in FastenMaster timber screws, steel post bases

tips.frame: Plumb and brace posts temporarily before marking mortise shoulders or cutting knee-brace compound miters.
general: Cut 45-degree brace heels with 1/2 in housing steps to transfer lateral thrust directly into solid wood.
Pre-drill pilot holes for heavy structural screws to prevent splitting cedar end-grain.

watchOut: Cedar splits easily near end distances; maintain minimum 3 in screw edge clearance.
Provide temporary diagonal cross-bracing until the primary knee braces are fully fastened.

steps.title: Anchor post bases to foundation
steps.detail: Lay out post locations with tape, drill into the concrete slab, and anchor the steel standoff bases with heavy wedge anchors.

steps.title: Erect and plumb 6x6 cedar posts
steps.detail: Seat the rough-sawn cedar posts into the standoff brackets, plumb each post in both axes, and secure with through-bolts.

steps.title: Set and fasten 6x10 header beam
steps.detail: Hoist the 6x10 cedar beam onto the post tenon seats, verifying equal 300 mm overhangs, then drive three structural timber screws down through the beam into each post cap.

steps.title: Install 4x4 diagonal knee braces
steps.detail: Snug the 45-degree knee braces against the post inside faces and header underside, then drive two 8-inch timber screws through pre-drilled counterbores at each mitered joint.

entries.name: Laboratory Chemical Epoxy Countertop & Cup Sink
entries.variant: 1 in monolithic modified epoxy resin top, coved epoxy marine edge, drop-in epoxy oval cup sink, acid-resistant drain
entries.material: 1 in monolithic epoxy resin, chemical-resistant 2-part epoxy adhesive, molded epoxy cup sink, polyolefin sink tailpiece

tips.frame: Level base casework perfectly using shims before placing heavy monolithic resin tops.
general: Clean resin joint edges with acetone and tape joint borders before applying color-matched two-part epoxy cement.
Smooth resin cement joints flush using a broad putty knife dipped in solvent before it hardens.

watchOut: Epoxy resin is brittle and exceptionally heavy; lift with glass suction cups and support full spans to avoid snapping.
Ensure the tailpiece and drain plumbing use acid-resistant polyolefin or borosilicate glass, not standard PVC.

parts.name: Left welded H-frame with leveling glides
Right welded H-frame with leveling glides
1 in monolithic epoxy resin countertop slab with cutout
Front coved epoxy marine containment edge

steps.title: Erect laboratory tubular steel base frame
steps.detail: Stand both welded end frames, bridge them with top and rear tubular stringers, and secure with structural hex through-bolts. Adjust the bottom leveling glides until the top frame rails sit true in both directions.

steps.title: Bed monolithic epoxy countertop slab
steps.detail: Apply continuous beads of chemical-resistant adhesive along top frame flanges and lower the 1 in thick epoxy slab onto the frame with the cup sink cutout positioned to the right.

steps.title: Bond marine containment edges and backsplash
steps.detail: Trowel mixed two-part black epoxy resin along perimeter rebates, bond the front and side marine curb strips flush to contain spills, and set the rear monolithic backsplash tight to the wall line.

steps.title: Bed drop-in epoxy cup sink into cutout
steps.detail: Butter the underside perimeter of the molded cup sink rim with chemical-resistant resin cement, seat the basin squarely into the prepared top opening, and tool the extruded joint flush.

steps.title: Install acid-resistant drain tailpiece and P-trap
steps.detail: Pass the polyolefin threaded strainer down through the sink outlet with gasket seals, thread on the 1-1/2 in tailpiece, and make up mechanical compression joints to the cleanout P-trap.

steps.title: Mount epoxy-coated gooseneck service turret
steps.detail: Drop the corrosion-resistant deck turret shank through the drilled faucet hole behind the cup sink, tighten the heavy locknut beneath the slab, and align the serrated spout over the basin center.

entries.name: Lead-Lined Drywall & Radiation Shielding
entries.variant: 1/16 in sheet lead laminated 5/8 in Type X gypsum and lead screw discs
entries.material: Lead-backed gypsum board, 20-ga steel studs, lead fastener discs, 2 in lead sheet batten strips

tips.frame: Space 20-gauge steel studs at 12 or 16 inches on center with heavy-duty track anchorage.
general: Adhere 2-inch wide vertical lead strips behind all drywall joints to maintain shielding continuity.
Cap every drywall screw head with lead tabs bedded in approved contact adhesive.

watchOut: Never pierce lead shielding for unlined electrical junction boxes or surface conduit without baffled lead backings.

steps.title: Erect 20-Gauge Steel Stud Partition
steps.desc: Anchor the top and bottom runner tracks, then friction-fit and fasten the 20-gauge steel studs at plumb intervals to carry heavy lead-shielded boarding.

steps.title: Affix 2-Inch Lead Batten Shield Strips
steps.desc: Adhere 2-inch wide 1/16-inch lead batten strips vertically to stud faces to provide seamless radiation attenuation behind drywall seams and screw paths.

steps.title: Hang Lead-Lined Type X Gypsum Panels
steps.desc: Lift and secure factory-laminated lead-lined drywall panels tight against framing with Type S drywall bugle head screws centered into the lead batten strip.

steps.title: Cap Screw Penetrations with Lead Discs
steps.desc: Install self-adhesive 1/16-inch sheet lead screw caps over all recessed fastener heads to eliminate radiation leakage through wall penetrations.

entries.name: Timber Wall Let-In 1x4 Diagonal Bracing
entries.variant: 2x4 stud wall at 16 in O.C., notched 1x4 SPF brace at 45-degree angle
entries.material: 2x4 SPF framing lumber, 1x4 SPF brace board, 8d common nails, 16d sinkers

tips.frame: Square the assembled wall on the deck using 3-4-5 triangulation before scoring the let-in brace lines.
general: Set circular saw depth precisely to 3/4 in to kerf the stud faces without weakening the wall cavity.
Chop kerfed notches clean with a sharp wood chisel so the 1x4 sits dead flush with stud faces.

watchOut: Over-cutting notch depth beyond 3/4 in violates structural stud net area requirements.
Braces must run continuously from top plate to bottom plate at roughly 45 to 60 degrees.

steps.title: Assemble sole plate and interior studs
steps.desc: Layout 2x4 studs on 16 inch centers along the sole plate. Face-nail each stud through the bottom of the plate using two 16d sinkers per connection.

steps.title: Fasten double top plate assembly
steps.desc: Position the lower top plate across the upper ends of the studs and end-nail with 16d sinkers. Lap the upper cap plate over the assembly and face-nail at 16 inches on center.

steps.title: Install diagonal 1x4 let-in brace
steps.desc: Square the wall diagonally, scribe the 1x4 path across stud faces at 45 degrees, and kerf mortises 3/4 inch deep. Embed the 1x4 flush and fasten with two 8d common nails at each stud intersection and three at the plates.

entries.name: Electrician: 48A EV Charger Hardwire Branch Assembly
entries.variant: 60A 2-pole breaker feed, 1 in PVC conduit, 6 AWG THHN, 60A disconnect switch
entries.material: 60A non-fusible AC disconnect, 1 in Schedule 40 PVC conduit, 6 AWG copper THHN conductors, Level 2 EVSE charging unit

tips.frame: Anchor disconnect box and EVSE base plate to backer board with 40 cm horizontal separation.
general: Size conductors at 125% of continuous load (48A load requires minimum 60A rated circuit and wiring).
Torque all terminal lugs to specified inch-pounds using a calibrated torque screwdriver and apply witness marks.

watchOut: Loose lug connections under sustained 48A continuous charging draw create thermal runaway and melt terminal blocks.
Ensure grounding conductor bonding inside the metallic disconnect complies with NEC 250 equipment grounding rules.

steps.title: Mount Backer Panel and EVSE Sub-Plate
steps.detail: Fasten 3/4 in plywood backing substrate flush to wall studs using wood screws. Position and plumb the EVSE steel mounting bracket on the right quadrant at 1020 mm center line.

steps.title: Install 60A Safety Disconnect and Supply Conduit
steps.detail: Secure 60A NEMA 3R non-fusible pullout disconnect to backer board. Route 1 in Schedule 40 PVC vertical feed conduit from floor line into bottom concentric knockout and clamp with two-hole straps.

steps.title: Connect Horizontal PVC Interconnect Raceway
steps.detail: Cut and ream 1 in Schedule 40 PVC nipple to 190 mm. Solvent weld into male terminal adapters and fasten with locknuts between the disconnect right knockout and the EVSE side entry knockout.

steps.title: Pull and Terminate 6 AWG THHN Conductors
steps.detail: Pull two 6 AWG black/red ungrounded copper conductors and one 8 AWG green equipment grounding conductor across the nipple. Land on disconnect load lugs and prepare charger input leads.

steps.title: Hang EVSE Charger and Mount Cable Holster
steps.detail: Hang the Level 2 EVSE charger enclosure onto the mounting bracket and torque field terminals. Fasten the cable dock holster beneath the charger, hang coiled 25 ft cord, and dock connector nozzle.

entries.name: Loading Dock Leveler Pit Curb Angle & Weld Plate Frame
entries.variant: 3x3x1/4 in pit edge steel curb angles, concrete anchor studs (8 in O.C.), embedded front channel weld plate
entries.material: 3x3x1/4 ASTM A36 steel angle, 1/2 in x 6 in headed shear studs, embedded C6 channel, rebar ties, weld plates

tips.frame: Erect braced plywood box forms inside the dock pit to hold embedded curb angles perfectly square and level.
general: Tie curb angle headed concrete anchors securely into the slab top rebar mat using tie wire prior to concrete pour.
Check pit diagonal cross-measurements frequently; pit squareness is critical for dock leveler ramp fitment.

watchOut: Curb angles that float or bow during concrete placement will prevent the mechanical or hydraulic leveler from dropping in.
Vibrate concrete thoroughly under curb angle horizontal legs to eliminate hollow air voids beneath heavy impact zones.

Left curb headed anchor studs (8 in OC)
Right curb headed anchor studs (8 in OC)
Left dock bumper weld plate with anchors
Right dock bumper weld plate with anchors

steps.title: Cast foundation slab and place rebar mat
steps.detail: Pour the reinforced concrete pit base slab and wire-tie the #4 rebar grid at required clearance above the subgrade.

steps.title: Set embedded front channel weld plate
steps.detail: Position the C6x8.2 channel along the front sill of the pit floor to serve as the embedded base anchor for the dock leveler hinge frame.

steps.title: Position rear curb angle with Nelson studs
steps.detail: Align the 3x3x1/4 rear curb angle along the back pit rim with headed shear studs projecting horizontally into the surrounding slab pour.

steps.title: Square and secure left and right curb angles
steps.detail: Miter and tack-weld side curb angles to the rear angle, ensuring pit diagonal dimensions are square within 1/8 inch before concrete placement.

steps.title: Embed front bumper mounting weld plates
steps.detail: Anchor heavy-gauge dock bumper weld plates flush with the dock face on both flanks of the pit opening to absorb truck impact forces.

entries.name: NEMA Motor Starter & 3-Wire Control Station
entries.variant: NEMA Size 1 starter, overload relay, remote START/STOP pushbutton station
entries.material: NEMA 1 starter enclosure, 120V holding coil, bimetal thermal overload, 22mm momentary pushbuttons, 14 AWG MTW wire

general: Wire holding coil contact (auxiliary contact 2-3) in parallel with normally open START button.
Connect normally closed STOP button in series ahead of the holding circuit loop.

watchOut: Size thermal overload heaters strictly according to motor full load amps (FLA) nameplate.
Lock out and tag out line side power before landing motor phase leads on T1, T2, T3.

steps.title: Erect the benchtop backboard
steps.detail: Fasten the vertical training panel securely to the slotted base support cleats using wood screws.

steps.title: Mount the starter tub and station box
steps.detail: Align and secure the NEMA 1 enclosure tub and remote pushbutton station box to the panel layout lines.

steps.title: Fit the interconnecting and service conduits
steps.detail: Install the horizontal EMT nipple between enclosures and secure line and load conduit nipples with locknuts.

steps.title: Install contactor, overload relay, and terminal block
steps.detail: Bolt the NEMA Size 1 contactor baseplate, close-couple the thermal overload unit, and seat the lower terminal block.

steps.title: Install START and STOP pushbuttons
steps.detail: Mount the 22mm momentary flush START operator and extended mushroom STOP operator through the station cover knockouts.

steps.title: Terminate 3-wire control circuit conductors
steps.detail: Wire the stop circuit in series with start button, coil terminal A1, and holding contact 2-3 seal-in circuit using 14 AWG MTW.

entries.name: Medical Gas Zone Valve Box & Gauge Assembly
entries.variant: Dual-service (Oxygen / MedVac) recessed box, NFPA 99 silver-brazed copper
entries.material: Recessed zone valve box, 3-piece bronze full-port ball valves, Type L/K degreased medical copper, BCuP-5 brazing alloy

tips.frame: Frame 16-gauge steel stud rough opening to accept flush aluminum valve cabinet.
general: Purge copper lines continuously with dry nitrogen during torch brazing to stop internal scale formation.
Ensure valve handles point down when open and lock clear of outer breakaway acrylic window.

watchOut: Never use flux on medical gas copper-to-copper joints; silver alloy brazing requires flux-free assembly.
Keep all medical pipe ends capped and degreased to eliminate organic explosion hazards in oxygen service.

parts.name: Oxygen lower inlet pipe stub (Type K)
Oxygen 3-piece bronze ball valve with green handle
Oxygen pressure gauge and demand check tee
MedVac lower inlet pipe stub (Type L)
MedVac 3-piece bronze ball valve with white handle
MedVac vacuum gauge and demand check tee
Breakaway transparent acrylic window with pull ring

steps.title: Erect rough framing and box support brackets
steps.detail: Anchor the bottom runner track to the slab and plumb the left and right structural studs. Fasten upper and lower mounting brackets across the studs at the specified NFPA zone valve height.

steps.title: Set and secure the recessed zone valve box
steps.detail: Slide the dual-service galvanized steel enclosure between the studs and fasten through the side flanges and mounting brackets, ensuring the box is square and level.

steps.title: Install Medical Oxygen valve train and gauge
steps.detail: Position the degreased Type K copper inlet and outlet risers through the rubber pipe grommets and align the 3-piece bronze ball valve and pressure gauge assembly.

steps.title: Install Medical Vacuum valve train and gauge
steps.detail: Mount the Medical Vacuum Type L copper inlet and outlet lines through the right-hand bay. Seat the vacuum ball valve and compound vacuum indicator tee securely in line.

steps.title: Fasten trim bezel and breakaway emergency window
steps.detail: Secure the finished aluminum perimeter trim frame around the drywall opening and clip in the clear breakaway acrylic window with the emergency pull ring positioned at the bottom.

entries.name: Modular Security Vault Interlocking Wall Panel
entries.variant: Class 1 composite steel vault panels, interlock tongue-and-groove joint, welded splice tie plate, anchor studs
entries.material: High-strength steel composite vault panels, ceramic aggregate slurry core, 1/2 in steel splice plates, wedge anchors

tips.frame: Check floor slab capacity and verify perimeter boundary lines before flying heavy modular panels into place.
general: Draw tongue and groove joints together using heavy hydraulic puller clamps until panel faces align flush.
Weld internal joiner clips along the joint using 7018 low-hydrogen electrodes per security specifications.

watchOut: Panels are extremely heavy (800+ lbs); rigging equipment must stay rigged until top stabilizing ties are welded.
Ensure structural anchoring into base slabs meets UL 608 burglary resistance depth requirements.

steps.title: Set and anchor floor embed channel
steps.detail: Align the base channel along the vault perimeter baseline and drive heavy wedge anchors into the concrete slab.

steps.title: Install base retainer angles
steps.detail: Affix base clip brackets to both flanges of the embed channel to establish guide stops for the composite panels.

steps.title: Rig and lower left vault panel
steps.detail: Lower the left composite panel squarely into the base channel using overhead rigging, ensuring plumb orientation.

steps.title: Interlock right vault panel
steps.detail: Position and slide the right panel into the channel, fully engaging the tongue into the adjacent panel's internal interlocking seam.

steps.title: Seat head restraint cap channel
steps.detail: Fit the continuous structural cap channel over the upper perimeter of the assembled panels to lock alignment.

steps.title: Mount vertical joint splice tie plates
steps.detail: Position heavy steel splice plates across the vertical interlock seam on both interior and exterior faces and torque tight prior to seam welding.

entries.name: Nail-Laminated Timber (NLT) Floor Decking with Glulam Ledger
entries.variant: 2x6 SPF laminations on edge, staggered 3-1/2 in framing nails at 12 in O.C., perimeter glulam support ledger
entries.material: #2 kiln-dried 2x6 lumber, 3-1/2 in ring-shank nails, 3-1/8 x 12 in glulam beam, structural ledger screws

tips.frame: Square the starting lamination perfectly against the girder bearing line and tack firmly with temporary end braces.
general: Stagger nail patterns high and low along the lamination face to prevent splitting the adjacent grain.
Clamp bowed 2x6 boards tightly to the preceding lamination using bar clamps or a heavy framing lever before driving nails.
Keep end butt joints staggered by at least four feet between adjacent lamination runs across the deck.

watchOut: Ensure lumber moisture content is below 15% to prevent severe lateral shrinkage gaps across the wide laminated plane.
Confirm ledger fasteners have full thread engagement into the solid core of the glulam girder.

steps.title: Set glulam support posts
steps.detail: Layout and plumb the four heavy timber support posts at front and rear bearing lines.

steps.title: Mount glulam ledgers with structural screws
steps.detail: Seat the glulam beam ledgers onto the posts and drive structural ledger screws through each connection point.

steps.title: Nail starter 2x6 laminations
steps.detail: Place 2x6 lumber on edge spanning between ledgers. Nail each successive lamination with 3-1/2 in ring-shank nails staggered at 12 in centres.

steps.title: Complete NLT decking field
steps.detail: Drive laminations tightly against adjacent plies using a sledge block and maintain staggered framing nail spacing across all laminations.

steps.title: Fasten perimeter glulam rim ledger
steps.detail: Align the perimeter glulam edge ledger flush with deck level and secure into the laminated timber core with structural screws.

entries.name: Open-Web Wood Floor Truss with Strongback Stiffener
entries.variant: 14 in deep wood-web metal-plated trusses at 19.2 in O.C., 2x6 vertical strongback
entries.material: 14 in open-web manufactured floor trusses, 2x6 SPF strongback ribbons, 2x4 bracing blocks, 16d duplex and common nails

tips.frame: Mark truss spacing accurately on both top plates and verify truss orientation tags before standing floor joists.
general: Orient strongback 2x6 vertically against web uprights near mid-span to distribute dynamic footfall loads across adjacent trusses.
Anchor strongback blocks securely to avoid floor squeaks and truss roll under construction staging.

watchOut: Never cut, drill, or notch any chord or metal plate of an engineered wood truss.
Walk only on fully braced chords; unbraced long-span trusses can buckle laterally without warning.

steps.title: Set bearing plates
steps.detail: Lay and level the 2x6 bearing sill plates parallel across the foundation line.

steps.title: Set open-web floor trusses
steps.detail: Stand the 14-inch manufactured open-web trusses at 19.2 inches on-center and toenail both chord ends to bearing plates.

steps.title: Install end rim boards
steps.detail: Fasten engineered rim boards flush against the exterior ends of the floor trusses to prevent rollover and transfer shear.

steps.title: Thread vertical strongback
steps.detail: Slide the continuous 2x6 strongback on edge through the truss web bays at midspan tight against the center vertical posts.

steps.title: Secure strongback bracing blocks
steps.detail: Fasten 2x4 blocking to the bottom chord tight against the vertical strongback to lock it firmly against dynamic floor deflection.

entries.name: Operable Partition Wall Overhead Track & Carrier
entries.variant: Heavy-duty aluminum track, dual horizontal steel trolley carriers, 3/8 in all-thread rods, drop seal mechanism
entries.material: Extruded aluminum overhead track, steel ball-bearing trolleys, 3/8 in B7 threaded rod, acoustical baffles, Unistrut

tips.frame: Laser-level Unistrut structural suspension headers to within 1/16 inch across the full opening width.
general: Suspend the track using double jam nuts on threaded rods to secure track elevation against vibration.
Pack dense acoustical mineral wool above the track header to maintain sound transmission class ratings.

watchOut: Out-of-level tracks cause heavy wall partition leaves to drift spontaneously and damage mechanical seals.
Ensure suspension all-thread ties directly into certified structural steel or joist anchors, not drywall framing.

steps.title: Anchor overhead Unistrut channel
steps.detail: Fasten structural angle clips to the overhead slab using expansion anchors, then bolt the Unistrut channel across the clips.

steps.title: Install threaded suspension rods
steps.detail: Thread 3/8-inch B7 rods into channel spring nuts seated within the Unistrut, securing each with top lock washers and hex nuts.

steps.title: Mount and level aluminum track
steps.detail: Slip track hanger clamps over the top flanges of the extruded track and torque double jam nuts to set laser-verified elevation.

steps.title: Fasten acoustical sound baffles
steps.detail: Secure dense acoustical plenum sound barriers along both sides of the overhead track cavity to prevent flanking noise.

steps.title: Insert steel trolley carriers
steps.detail: Roll dual steel ball-bearing trolleys into the track throat and suspend high-tensile pendant bolts with safety locking nuts.

steps.title: Hang partition header and drop seal
steps.detail: Couple panel mounting brackets to the carrier pendant bolts, securing the top header extrusion and integral drop seal mechanism.

entries.name: Parapet Wall Framing with Diagonal Joist Kickers
entries.variant: 2x6 studs extending 36 in above roof deck, 2x4 diagonal kickers at 48 in O.C.
entries.material: 2x6 exterior SPF studs, 2x4 SPF kickers, 1/2 in CDX roof deck, Simpson CS16 coil strapping, 16d galvanized nails

tips.frame: Extend exterior balloon studs past roof rim framing rather than building a hinged hinge-joint knee wall where possible.
general: Anchor diagonal kicker braces back into roof joist blocking at a 45-degree angle to resist cantilevered wind loads.
Slope the parapet top plate 1/4 inch per foot toward the roof drain field to shed standing water.

watchOut: Inadequate kicker fastening allows the parapet cap to flex in storms, cracking the exterior coping.
Always set up fall arrest harnesses when working along outer parapet edges.

steps.title: Frame the exterior parapet wall
steps.detail: Lay out the 2x6 sole plate, stand all six studs at 16 in. on-centre, and cap with staggered double top plates nailed with 16d common nails.

steps.title: Install roof ledger and rear support framing
steps.detail: Fasten the 2x8 ledger board to the inside face of the parapet studs and erect the rear stub wall and rim joist parallel to the wall.

steps.title: Hang the roof joists
steps.detail: Place 2x8 SPF roof joists at 16 in. on-centre between the ledger and the rear rim board, aligning joist positions with kicker studs.

steps.title: Fasten roof sheathing
steps.detail: Fasten 1/2 in. CDX plywood across the roof joists tight to the inside parapet stud faces, nailing at 6 in. edge spacing.

steps.title: Install 2x4 diagonal kickers
steps.detail: Cut 2x4 diagonal braces at 45 degrees and nail them at 48 in. on-centre, sistering each brace from the upper parapet stud down to the roof framing.

steps.title: Apply Simpson CS16 coil strapping
steps.detail: Install Simpson CS16 continuous tension straps along the diagonal kickers and vertical tension ties across the roof plane to resist outward cantilever wind forces.

entries.name: Pre-Engineered Building Rod X-Brace & Hillside Washer
entries.variant: 7/8 in threaded structural rod, ductile iron hillside washer, structural steel column web punch, drop-forged turnbuckle
entries.material: ASTM A36 7/8 in steel rod, ductile hillside washers, heavy hex nuts, forged steel turnbuckle body, zinc primer

tips.frame: Plumb primary steel columns with transit lasers before tensioning diagonal rod brace networks.
general: Seat the curved bearing shoulder of the ductile hillside washer squarely in the column web slotted hole.
Rotate the center turnbuckle barrel evenly until all catenary sag is removed and specified rod pretension is reached.

watchOut: Uneven over-tightening of cross braces pulls building columns out of plumb and twists column flanges.
Always install and tighten secondary jamb jam-nuts against the turnbuckle body to prevent rotational backing-out.
