steps.detail: Position and fillet-weld the lower gusset plates to the inside faces of both column bases to receive the slotted brace ends.

steps.title: Land and bolt paired HSS 4x4 chevron braces
steps.detail: Slide the slotted ends of the paired HSS 4x4 diagonal braces over the top and bottom gussets, align bolt holes with spud wrenches, and torque A325 fasteners.

entries.name: Structural Steel Column Splice with Flange & Web Plates
entries.variant: W14x120 to W14x90 column transition, 1/2 in flange splice plates, web splice plates, filler shims, 7/8 in A490 TC bolts
entries.material: W14 structural steel column sections, 1/2 in Grade 50 steel splice plates, A490 tension-control bolts, mill shims

tips.frame: Plumb and center the lower column stub on anchor bolts before landing and pinning the upper tier column.
general: Insert fill plates between different column depths to maintain proper clamping without bending the splice plates.
Use drift pins in opposite corners to bring bolt holes into precise concentric alignment before running bolts.
Tighten tension-control bolts starting from the most rigid center row outward until the spline ends shear off.

watchOut: Never remove the crane hoisting line until at least two bolts per flange connection are fully pinned or snugged.
Inspect bolt threads and washers to ensure hardened washers are placed under the turned element per RCSC specification.

steps.title: Position and plumb lower W14x120 column
steps.detail: Erect the lower heavy column tier onto baseplate anchors, plumb both principal axes, and check milling squareness at the top splice plane.

steps.title: Land upper W14x90 column onto bearing splice
steps.detail: Lower the lighter tier onto the milled joint, aligning column centerlines to maintain continuous load path and checking bearing contact.

steps.title: Install web and flange transition filler shims
steps.detail: Place 8 mm flange shims and 2 mm web shims on the upper tier to compensate for profile depth and thickness differences.

steps.title: Mount web splice plates
steps.detail: Sandwich the column webs with dual 10 mm splice plates centered across the joint line and pin alignment holes using spud wrenches.

steps.title: Fit outer flange splice plates
steps.detail: Position 1/2 in thick splice plates tight against the outer flange faces, bridging the seam between lower and upper tiers.

steps.title: Install and snug 7/8 in web splice bolts
steps.detail: Insert tension-control bolts through the web plates and shims, bringing all fasteners to initial snug-tight condition from center outward.

steps.title: Install and torque flange tension-control bolts
steps.detail: Insert 7/8 in A490 TC bolts across both flange plates and shear off the splines using an electric shear wrench to complete the rigid splice.

entries.name: Structural Steel Beam-to-Column Seat Angle Joint
entries.variant: W12x30 column flange, W14x22 floor girder, 6x4x1/2 in seat angle
entries.material: W12x30 wide-flange column, W14x22 beam, L6x4x1/2 steel angles, 3/4 in ASTM A325 high-strength structural bolts

tips.frame: Set seat angle level and verify column flange centerlines prior to torquing the lower bearing angle bolts.
general: Land beam lower flange squarely onto the seat angle before installing the flexible top stability angle.
Perform snug-tight inspection on all A325 structural bolts before turning of the nut procedure.

watchOut: Never release crane rigging hook until at least two bolts per connection are installed wrench-tight.
Watch for finger pinch points when lowering heavy structural beams onto the bottom shelf angle.

steps.title: Set the column base plate
steps.detail: Position the 1-inch steel base plate over the foundation anchor studs and level using leveling nuts.

steps.title: Erect the W12x30 column
steps.detail: Hoist and land the wide-flange column onto the base plate, plumbing the column with shims before tightening anchor nuts.

steps.title: Bolt the L6x4 seat angle to the column
steps.detail: Mount the unstiffened seat angle with its 6-inch vertical leg against the column flange using four 3/4-inch A325 structural bolts.

steps.title: Land the girder and fasten the seat
steps.detail: Lower the W14x22 floor girder onto the 4-inch outstanding leg of the seat angle leaving a 1/2-inch erection gap, then install bottom flange bolts.

steps.title: Install top stability clip angle
steps.detail: Fit the L4x4 stability angle over the top flange of the beam and column face, torquing all four ASTM A325 high-strength bolts snug-tight.

entries.name: Submersible Sump Basin & Dual Check Discharge
entries.variant: 18x22 in poly basin, 1/2 HP pump, 1-1/2 in PVC, quiet check & ball valve
entries.material: Polyethylene sump basin with gasketed lid, 1/2 HP cast iron pump, 1-1/2 in Sch 40 PVC, rubber compression check valve

general: Drill a 3/16 in weep hole in discharge pipe between pump outlet and check valve to prevent airlock.
Set vertical float switch rod with adequate clearance so it cannot hang up on basin walls.

watchOut: Check valve arrows must point upwards with flow to prevent continuous water hammer cycling.
Plug sump pump into a dedicated GFCI-protected simplex receptacle; never use extension cords.

parts.name: Quiet spring check valve with rubber boots
1-1/2 in true union PVC ball valve

steps.title: Set the sump pit basin
steps.detail: Bed the polyethylene basin flat and level on washed aggregate at basement rough grade.

steps.title: Install the pump and lower discharge
steps.detail: Seat the 1/2 HP pump on the basin floor, solvent weld the 1-1/2 inch PVC riser into the male discharge adapter, and drill a 3/16 inch weep hole.

steps.title: Fasten lid and penetration seals
steps.detail: Lower the gasketed lid over the discharge pipe, fit radon seal grommets into the discharge and vent ports, and bolt down the perimeter rim.

steps.title: Mount the check valve and shut-off valve
steps.detail: Clamp the compression check valve over the lower pipe stub and solvent weld the short spool into the true union ball valve.

steps.title: Run upper discharge and vent risers
steps.detail: Glue the upper discharge stack into the ball valve outlet and seat the 2-inch vent stack through the lid grommet.

entries.name: Tankless Water Heater Isolation Valve Rough-In
entries.variant: 3/4 in copper service kit, pressure relief valve, concentric poly vent
entries.material: Type L copper tubing, tankless isolation valves, 150 PSI brass PRV, 3/4 in gas ball valve, 2x4 framing

tips.frame: Anchor 3/4-inch CDX plywood backer board between studs to bear hanging bracket.
general: Sweat copper adapters prior to threading onto tankless isolation valves to avoid burning EPDM seals.
Run PRV blow-off pipe full size downwards terminating within 6 inches of floor drain.

watchOut: Do not install shutoff valves between the pressure relief valve and heater core.
Ensure combustion intake/exhaust pipes maintain manufacturer-mandated pitch back to unit drain.

parts.name: 3/4 in black iron gas supply riser
3/4 in Type L copper cold riser
3/4 in cold isolation valve with purge port
3/4 in hot isolation valve with PRV tap
3/4 in Type L copper hot distribution drop

steps.title: Frame wall backing rough opening
steps.detail: End-nail top and sole plates to the vertical 2x4 studs with two 16d common nails per joint.

steps.title: Fasten equipment backer board
steps.detail: Square and screw the 3/4-inch plywood backer across the studs to provide a rigid mechanical ground for the heater and piping.

steps.title: Hang tankless water heater and vent collar
steps.detail: Mount the tankless unit bracket to the backer board and slip the concentric polypropylene flue adapter onto the top outlet collar.

steps.title: Rough in the gas supply train
steps.detail: Thread the 3/4-inch gas shut-off valve to the black iron riser, then tie in the appliance connector nipple directly into the unit gas inlet.

steps.title: Install water isolation kit and relief valve
steps.detail: Thread the color-coded isolation valves to the cold inlet and hot outlet spuds, mount the 150 PSI relief valve, and extend the discharge pipe toward the floor drain.

entries.name: Acoustical Wall: Beveled Snap-Track & Fabric
entries.variant: 1 in high-density fiberglass board with perimeter PVC gripper track
entries.material: 1 in 6 pcf fiberglass acoustic board, PVC snap jaw tracking, acoustic polyester fabric, 1/2 in staples

tips.frame: Miter perimeter polymer snap-tracks at 45 degrees and staple/screw to drywall backing along layout lines.
general: Impale semi-rigid fiberglass core inside the tracks using spray contact adhesive.
Tuck fabric into the locking jaws working systematically from center outward using a rock-in spatula.

watchOut: Keep fabric weave lines straight and square while tensioning to avoid visible wavy distortion.

steps.title: Position Wall Substrate
steps.desc: Plumb and align the 1/2-inch drywall substrate panel squarely on the mounting plane.

steps.title: Fasten Horizontal Snap Tracks
steps.desc: Anchor the top and bottom beveled PVC gripper tracks horizontally flush against the backer board with drywall screws spaced along each track.

steps.title: Fasten Vertical Perimeter Snap Tracks
steps.desc: Butt vertical snap tracks between the top and bottom rails and secure firmly with screws spaced along the left and right edges.

steps.title: Set Acoustic Core Board
steps.desc: Press-fit the 1-inch 6 pcf high-density fiberglass board snugly inside the perimeter tracking cavity flush against the backing board.

steps.title: Stretch and Lock Acoustic Fabric
steps.desc: Align fabric over the acoustic board and tuck edges progressively into the beveled PVC snap jaw track for a drum-tight acoustic finish.

entries.name: Electrician: 3-Way & 4-Way Switching Branch Circuit
entries.variant: 15A 120V circuit, dual 3-way switches, one 4-way switch, keyless fixture
entries.material: 14/2 and 14/3 NM-B copper cable, single-gang fiberglass boxes, 3-way and 4-way toggles, porcelain lamp holder

tips.frame: Mount rough-in device boxes at 120 cm center height across stud bays spaced 40 cm apart.
general: Tag common screw terminals with black electrical tape immediately when stripping the 14/3 traveler jacket.
Ensure neutral wires are spliced continuously through all switch boxes to comply with modern NEC neutral-at-switch rules.

watchOut: Swapping a traveler conductor with a common terminal will cause erratic switching or dead dead-zones.
Pigtail all equipment ground conductors inside each box directly to switch ground screws.

steps.title: Frame Training Partition and Blocking
steps.text: Erect studs at standard 600 mm centers between top and bottom plates. Fasten horizontal blocking in bay 4 to rigidly support the luminaire outlet box.

steps.title: Rough-In Device and Fixture Enclosures
steps.text: Nail single-gang switch boxes at standard switch height centered on layout studs. Anchor the octagonal junction box flush to the face of bay 4 fixture blocking.

steps.title: Pull Branch Feed and Traveler Cables
steps.text: Route 14/2 line feed into switch box 1, 14/3 traveler cables between switches, and 14/2 switch leg up to the luminaire box. Secure runs with insulated framing staples within 200 mm of each box.

steps.title: Terminate 3-Way and 4-Way Toggle Switches
steps.text: Terminate line hot to the dark common screw on switch 1, cross travelers through the input and output pairs of the 4-way switch, and land travelers onto switch 2 with common feeding the switch leg.

steps.title: Install Porcelain Lampholder and Lamp
steps.text: Connect the switch leg hot conductor to the brass center-contact terminal and neutral conductor to the nickel shell terminal. Fasten the lamp base to the box and thread in the test lamp.

entries.name: Ground Anchor Tieback Bearing Plate & Wedge Head
entries.variant: 4-strand 0.6 in tendon bundle, 12x12x1.5 in beveled bearing plate, 4-hole wedge anchor head
entries.material: High-strength 7-wire strand tendons, 1-1/2 in ASTM A36 beveled bearing plate, trumpeted guide pipe, 3-part wedge grips

tips.frame: Align trumpet pipe and bearing plate exactly square to the tendon drill angle to eliminate eccentric bending stresses.
general: Clean rust and slurry from strand tails before feeding them through anchor head wedge cavities.
Seat 3-part serrated steel wedges evenly into tapered holes using a spring-loaded seating tool before hydraulic ram tensioning.

watchOut: Never stand directly in line behind the anchor head during proof testing or final tension lock-off.
Coat exposed strand ends and wedge cavity with corrosion-inhibiting petrolatum grease inside the threaded steel protection cap.

steps.title: Set reaction block and trumpet sleeve
steps.detail: Cast the soldier wall reaction block and bed the steel trumpeted sleeve flush to maintain drill hole alignment.

steps.title: Feed 4-strand tendon bundle
steps.detail: Insert the 4 high-strength 0.6-inch strands up through the trumpet pipe, keeping bundles parallel and untwisted.

steps.title: Install beveled bearing plate
steps.detail: Slide the 12x12x1.5-inch ASTM A36 beveled bearing plate over the bundle, seating it firmly against the trumpet flange.

steps.title: Mount 4-hole wedge anchor head
steps.detail: Thread the tendon bundle through the 4 matching tapered pockets of the cylindrical steel anchor head and seat it centered on the plate.

steps.title: Seat 3-part wedge grips
steps.detail: Snap the 3-piece wedge assemblies around each strand and seat them with a seating tool ready for hydraulic stressing.

entries.name: Heavy Timber Hammer Beam Roof Truss Bracket Assembly
entries.variant: 8x10 horizontal hammer beam, 8x8 hammer post, curved 6x8 knee brace, traditional mortise-and-tenon joints with oak dowels
entries.material: Select Structural Douglas fir timbers, 1 in kiln-dried red oak draw-bore pegs, anchor tie rods, timber wax

tips.frame: Test-fit all mortise-and-tenon joints dry on sawhorses using test pins before raising the assembly into vertical position.
general: Offset peg holes by 1/8 in through the tenon (draw-boring) to pull the shoulder tightly closed as oak pegs are driven.
Chamfer the lead end of wood pegs and drive them with a wooden mallet, trimming flush after final seating.
Install a curved timber strut under the cantilevered hammer beam to transfer roof outward thrust safely down to the wall post.

watchOut: Hammer beam trusses generate extreme lateral outward thrust; external buttresses or tie rods are structurally necessary.
Check timber moisture content; green timber shrinkage can loosen peg draw-bore tension over time.

parts.name: External steel tie rod anchor plate
Heavy hex tension rod end and washer
Oak draw-bore pegs at wall post tenon
Oak draw-bore peg at lower brace heel
Oak draw-bore peg at lower brace head
Oak draw-bore peg at hammer post base
Oak draw-bore peg at collar joint

steps.title: Set stone corbel and erect principal wall post
steps.detail: Bed the stone template pad on high-strength grout and plumb the vertical Douglas fir wall post and wall plate.

steps.title: Cantilever the hammer beam and fit wall anchors
steps.detail: Slide the horizontal 8x10 hammer beam tenon into the wall post pocket, pass through-bolts, and lock with the exterior steel bearing plate.

steps.title: Install the lower knee brace and draw-bore pegs
steps.detail: Seat the 6x8 knee brace into the mortises beneath the cantilever and draw-bore home kiln-dried 1-inch red oak pegs.

steps.title: Erect hammer post and attach decorative drop pendant
steps.detail: Tenon the 8x8 hammer post into the hammer beam top face, drive oak retaining pegs, and fit the carved pendant underneath.

steps.title: Pitch and seat the principal rafter
steps.detail: Crane the sloped principal rafter onto birdsmouth seats over the wall plate and hammer post head, aligning traditional mortise connections.

steps.title: Lock collar beam and upper arch brace
steps.detail: Drive the upper collar tie and curved arch brace home, locking all remaining tenons with waxed red oak dowels.

entries.name: Heavy Timber Mortise-and-Tenon Post-and-Beam Bent
entries.variant: 8x8 Douglas fir post and tie beam, 2 in thick tenon, 1 in red oak peg
entries.material: Rough-sawn 8x8 FOHC Douglas fir, turned 1 in white oak trunnels, anchor wax end sealer

tips.frame: Lay out joints from reference face and reference edge lines rather than rough sawn exterior dimensions.
general: Offset the drawbore hole in the tenon 1/8 inch closer to the shoulder to pull the joint tight upon driving the oak trunnel.
Check tenon shoulder squareness with a knife score line before making final hand-saw shoulder cuts.

watchOut: Do not overdrive dry hardwood pegs with a heavy iron sledge; use a dead-blow mallet to avoid grain fracturing.
Heavy timber components must be supported on horses with secure chocks to prevent roll-off injuries.

steps.title: Set and level the cross sill
steps.detail: Lay the 8x8 Douglas fir sill beam flat on the layout line and verify cross-grain and longitudinal level before framing.

steps.title: Erect and plumb the vertical posts
steps.detail: Seat the bottom tenons of both 8x8 posts into the sill mortises. Use a heavy wooden commander to drive the shoulders tight and brace upright.

steps.title: Fit the diagonal knee braces
steps.detail: Angle the 4x6 braces at 45 degrees and house their lower tenons into the mortises cut along the inner faces of the posts.

steps.title: Lower and seat the tie beam
steps.detail: Hoist the 8x8 tie beam over the post tenons and knee brace upper tenons. Drive downward evenly until all shoulders close flush.

steps.title: Drawbore and drive oak trunnels
steps.detail: Align drawbore holes using a tapered pod auger, then drive 1 in turned white oak trunnels through all mortise joints and trim relish flush.

entries.name: Heavy Timber Post-to-Beam Welded Saddle Connection
entries.variant: 6x6 solid Douglas fir post, 6x10 beam, 1/4 in steel column saddle cap
entries.material: 6x6 dressed Douglas fir post, 6x10 timber girder, welded 1/4 in powder-coated steel saddle bracket, 5/8 in galvanized bolts

tips.frame: Plumb the 6x6 post in two planes and brace securely with temporary 2x4 kickers before lowering the saddle cap.
general: Drill bolt holes using an auger bit guided by a drilling block to guarantee straight, parallel bores through 6-inch timber.
Drop the 6x10 beam squarely into the saddle throat and snug through-bolts with heavy flat washers.

watchOut: Do not notch beam bottom edges over saddle welds; bevel the wood beam corners slightly to maintain flat contact.
Secure timber beams from rolling or dislodging during erection until joists or knee braces are tied in.

parts.name: 1/4 in welded steel saddle cap bracket

steps.title: Set the pier and standoff post base
steps.detail: Center the standoff base bracket over the concrete pedestal anchor and torque securely.

steps.title: Erect and pin the timber post
steps.detail: Seat the 6x6 post onto the 1-inch standoff plate, plumb both faces, and insert the 5/8-inch through-bolt.

steps.title: Install welded saddle cap bracket
steps.detail: Slide the saddle cap downward over the column head until the seat plate rests flush on the end grain, then bolt through the post tabs.

steps.title: Position the 6x10 timber girder
steps.detail: Lower the timber girder into the saddle channel until it bears fully against the bottom plate.

steps.title: Through-bolt girder into saddle cap
steps.detail: Drill through pre-punched saddle flange holes and fasten the girder with four 5/8-inch galvanized bolts and heavy washers.

entries.name: Traditional Heavy Timber Under-Squinted Scarf Joint
entries.variant: 8x8 solid timber beam, under-squinted butt shoulders, hardwood central key
entries.material: 8x8 Douglas fir beams, dense white oak key wedge, 3/4 in galvanized threaded through-bolts with malleable iron washers

tips.frame: Establish a scarf joint length equal to at least 2.5 times the beam depth to ensure adequate horizontal shear resistance.
general: Cut under-squinted bevel shoulders at 15 degrees to lock beam ends firmly against vertical deflection.
Drive the central tapered hardwood wedge to force matching halving laps tightly into longitudinal compression.

watchOut: Check bolt hole clearances; excessive drift tolerance allows the timber joint to slip under dead load.
Never place a structural timber scarf splice at peak mid-span bending; locate joints near inflection points.

parts.name: Lower timber beam with under-squinted lap
Upper timber beam with under-squinted lap
Dense white oak front folding key wedge
Dense white oak rear folding key wedge

steps.title: Set assembly bolsters
steps.detail: Lay the heavy timber cribbing blocks level and parallel on the deck to support the scarf halves during layout and assembly.

steps.title: Seat the lower receiving timber
steps.detail: Position the left timber beam atop the bolsters with its under-squinted half-lap table facing upward.

steps.title: Drop and interlock the upper timber
steps.detail: Lower the mating timber carefully into position, locking the under-squinted butt shoulders together and aligning the central key mortise.

steps.title: Drive the hardwood folding keys
steps.detail: Insert the opposing white oak wedges into the transverse mortise and drive them alternately to draw the scarf shoulders dead tight.

steps.title: Install and torque through-bolts
steps.detail: Pass the 3/4-inch threaded bolts through the pre-bored vertical holes, seat the malleable iron washers, and tighten hex nuts with a wrench.

entries.name: Tongue & Groove Wood Ceiling: Blind-Nailed V-Joint Planking
entries.variant: 1x6 T&G white pine, 18-ga brad blind-nailed at 45°, 16 in O.C. framing
entries.material: 1x6 tongue-and-groove v-joint pine planks, 18-ga x 1-1/2 in brad nails, PVA wood glue, cove trim molding

tips.frame: Snap a center layout line across ceiling joists to ensure equal plank widths at opposing perimeter walls.
general: Install planks with the groove facing the starting wall and the tongue pointing in the direction of work progress.
Drive 18-ga brads at a 45-degree angle through the base of the tongue into every ceiling joist.

watchOut: Do not hammer directly on the wood tongue; always use an offcut grooved tapping block to seat boards snug.
Allow a 1/2 in expansion gap along all perimeter walls, concealed later behind perimeter crown or cove molding.

steps.title: Assemble ceiling framing grid
steps.detail: Lay out ceiling joists at 16 inches on center between the north and south header joists. End-nail two 16d framing nails through each header into each joist core.

steps.title: Set and blind-nail starter plank
steps.detail: Orient the grooved edge toward the wall with a 6 mm expansion gap. Face-nail the outer edge and blind-nail through the tongue at a 45-degree angle into every joist using 18-ga brads.

steps.title: Install first section of T&G field planking
steps.detail: Engage the female groove of each plank over the previous tongue, tapping tightly with a sacrificial wood block. Blind-nail through each tongue into each of the five framing joists.

steps.title: Continue planking across ceiling span
steps.detail: Continue driving planks across the ceiling bay, checking periodically for parallel alignment to the south header. Blind-nail each plank at every joist intersection.

steps.title: Scribe and blind-nail final closure plank
steps.detail: Rip the final board to width allowing for the perimeter expansion gap. Engage the joint with a pry bar and face-nail along the wall line where trim will cover.

steps.title: Install perimeter cove molding
steps.detail: Miter the cove molding corners at 45 degrees and pin through the ceiling planks into the perimeter backing members every 300 mm.

entries.name: Linen & Trash Chute Intake Door with Fusible Link
entries.variant: 15x18 in bottom-hinged 16-ga stainless hopper door, 165°F UL fusible link release, 1.5-hr B-label rated frame
entries.material: 16-ga 304 stainless steel intake door, steel mounting buck, 165°F fusible link assembly, expansion anchors

tips.frame: Square the heavy steel rough buck inside the masonry or shaft-wall opening before tightening anchors.
general: Mount the bottom-hinged stainless door assembly into the buck with heavy-gauge tamper-proof machine screws.
Connect the pneumatic closer mechanism and test self-closing and positive self-latching operation.

watchOut: Do not bypass or paint over the UL-listed fusible link; paint changes the melting point and voids fire safety ratings.
Ensure the intake throat transitions smoothly downward into the riser chute without projecting sharp edges or screw points.

steps.title: Set and anchor the throat buck sleeve
steps.detail: Slide the heavy-gauge chute throat sleeve into the wall rough opening and anchor through pre-punched jamb slots into the masonry rough buck.

steps.title: Install the 1.5-hr B-label trim frame
steps.detail: Fasten the satin stainless face frame and intumescent perimeter fire seal flush against the finished shaft wall.

steps.title: Hang the hopper door on the continuous hinge
steps.detail: Align the bottom piano hinge barrel between the frame sill and door leaf, then drive stainless machine screws to secure the bottom pivot.

steps.title: Attach the hydraulic closer cylinder
steps.detail: Pin the hydraulic closer body to the inner buck mounting bracket and link the piston rod to the hopper cheek plate.

steps.title: Mount the latch and 165°F fusible link kit
steps.detail: Fasten the ADA T-handle lockset into the door prep and install the UL-listed 165°F fusible link release at the top header catch.

entries.name: HVAC: VAV Terminal Box with Electric Reheat Coil
entries.variant: 8 in round inlet VAV box, damper motor, 2 kW electric duct heater, slip & drive
entries.material: 22-ga galvanized sheet metal casing, pneumatic/electronic damper actuator, open-coil electric reheat duct heater, S-cleat joints

tips.frame: Suspend VAV unit using four 3/8 in threaded rods, rubber vibration isolators, and unistrut trapeze cradles.
general: Provide at least 3 diameters of straight duct upstream of the velocity flow pickup ring to eliminate turbulence errors.
Connect discharge transitions to the electric reheat coil casing using tight-fitted drive cleats and self-drilling screws.

watchOut: Operating electric heating elements without confirmed airflow will trip thermal safeties and burn out nickel-chrome coils.
Seal all duct seams with mastic or approved foil tape; air leakage at VAV terminal ruins zone control.

steps.title: Assemble Trapeze Support Frame
steps.desc: Suspend four 3/8-inch threaded rods and secure two 1-5/8-inch Unistrut trapeze channels with hex nuts and square washers.

steps.title: Set VAV Terminal Box onto Trapeze Bearers
steps.desc: Rest the 22-gauge galvanized VAV casing squarely atop the trapeze cross members and verify level alignment.

steps.title: Install 8-Inch Inlet Collar and Flow Cross Sensor
steps.desc: Mount the round inlet collar and internal differential pressure airflow sensor cross onto the box primary air inlet.

steps.title: Mount Damper Actuator and DDC Controller
steps.desc: Slide the direct-coupled rotary damper actuator over the shaft and fasten the BACnet digital terminal controller to the cabinet face.

steps.title: Connect Electric Reheat Coil with S and Drive Cleats
steps.desc: Position the 2 kW electric reheat section to the discharge flanged opening using top and bottom S-cleats and vertical drive slips.

steps.title: Install Reheat Electrical Control Enclosure
steps.desc: Attach the heater control enclosure housing magnetic contactors, primary thermal cutoff, and safety airflow switch.

steps.title: Attach Rectangular Discharge Duct Extension
steps.desc: Fasten the downstream discharge duct transition onto the reheat discharge flange with sheet metal screws.

entries.name: Decorative Venetian Plaster: Multi-Coat Burnished Lime
entries.variant: Quartz primer substrate, 2 base coats, ultra-fine lime putty topcoat
entries.material: Slaked lime putty plaster, silica sand primer, carnauba wax, stainless steel burnishing trowel

tips.frame: Apply a uniform grit primer over a Level 4 drywall surface to establish mechanical keying.
general: Keep the stainless steel trowel edges rounded and polished to prevent razor gouges in wet plaster.
Burnish the final coat while still tacky by holding the trowel blade at a low 15-degree angle under firm pressure.

watchOut: Hydrated slaked lime is caustic; wear splash goggles and nitrile gloves throughout mixing and troweling.
Avoid dry-edge lap lines by maintaining a wet working edge across continuous wall planes.

steps.title: Erect stud wall substrate mock-up
steps.detail: Assemble the sole and top plates with four vertical 2x4 studs spaced across the 1200 mm width.

steps.title: Hang gypsum backer board
steps.detail: Fasten 1/2 in gypsum board flush to the stud faces to create a rigid, flat substrate.

steps.title: Roll silica quartz bonding primer
steps.detail: Apply coarse quartz primer leaving the bottom 400 mm exposed for stepped layer inspection.

steps.title: Trowel first lime basecoat (Grosso)
steps.detail: Spread slaked lime putty with coarse marble aggregate at 1.5 to 2 mm thickness across the primed area.

steps.title: Apply second lime intermediate coat (Medio)
steps.detail: Float a medium-aggregate lime putty coat over the cured basecoat to level minor hollows.

steps.title: Skim ultra-fine Grassello finish coat
steps.detail: Apply micro-thin coats of aged Grassello lime putty using tight, overlapping spatula strokes.

steps.title: Burnish finish and apply carnauba wax
steps.detail: Burnish the dried lime with the stainless steel trowel, then seal and buff with carnauba wax.

entries.name: Traditional Wall Wainscoting: Raised Stiles & Picture Frames
entries.variant: 1/2 in MDF stiles/rails, 1-3/8 in panel bolection molding, profile chair rail
entries.material: 1/2 x 4 in MDF stiles and rails, 1-3/8 in solid pine panel molding, 3-1/2 in chair rail, 18-ga brads, polyurethane adhesive

tips.frame: Level and snap a continuous chair rail datum line, then calculate equal panel box widths across wall bays.
general: Fasten horizontal base and top rails first, then space vertical stiles using a precision cut story stick.
Cut inside 45-degree miters on panel molding frames and test-fit corners with spring miter clamps before nailing.

watchOut: Locate all wall electrical receptacles early; never allow a vertical stile to bisect an outlet box or switch plate.
Glue and micro-pin all mitered panel corners to prevent seams from separating during thermal shrinkage.

steps.title: Establish datum and wall substrate
steps.detail: Snap level chalk lines across the wall studs and establish reference heights for bottom and top rails.

steps.title: Fasten horizontal MDF rails
steps.detail: Apply construction adhesive beads to the back of the bottom and top rails. Level and nail into wall studs with 18-gauge brads.

steps.title: Install vertical MDF stiles
steps.detail: Set the outer perimeter stiles plumb, then space the three intermediate stiles equally across the span and tack with brads.

steps.title: Fit bolection molding picture frames
steps.detail: Fit pre-mitred pine bolection moulding assemblies inside each bay, bedding in polyurethane adhesive and pin nailing into the stiles.

steps.title: Cap with chair rail and base shoe
steps.detail: Install the profiled chair rail directly over the top rail lip and secure base shoe molding tightly along the floor line.

entries.name: Walk-In Freezer Cam-Lock Panel Corner Joint
entries.variant: 4 in polyurethane foam core panels, male-female cam locks, PVC thermal break trim, butyl bead
entries.material: 4 in embossed steel IMP panels, internal hex cam locks, food-grade silicone sealant, butyl tape, PVC cove

tips.frame: Establish a square floor perimeter chalk line and level screed channels before seating wall panels.
general: Run continuous double beads of butyl sealant inside tongue-and-groove panel pockets before interlocking.
Engage internal cam-locks progressively from bottom to top using an Allen hex wrench until fully seated.

watchOut: Missing or discontinuous vapor seals allow humid ambient air infiltration, creating destructive interior ice buildup.
Do not overtighten cam-locks to avoid stripping the internal zinc cast gear mechanisms inside the foam.

steps.title: Anchor floor screed channels
steps.detail: Lay out the galvanized base channels square to chalk lines and fasten into the slab with concrete masonry anchors.

steps.title: Erect corner return panel
steps.detail: Seat the side wall panel into the base channel, checking vertical plumb on both internal and external faces.

steps.title: Apply vapor seal and mate butt panel
steps.detail: Apply dual continuous butyl sealant beads along the joint edge, then seat the mating back wall panel flush into the corner.

steps.title: Engage cam-locks and seal access ports
steps.detail: Insert the 5/16-inch hex wrench into internal access ports to rotate cam-locks until fully clamped, then snap in flush plastic plugs.

steps.title: Fasten exterior corner flashing
steps.detail: Fit the white embossed corner cap over the exterior corner seam and secure through panel skins with self-drilling screws.

steps.title: Install interior sanitary coves
steps.detail: Snap the vertical cove trim into the 90-degree corner and install the floor base coving to meet NSF food-safety standards.

entries.name: Horizontal Fire-Blocking & Mid-Wall Cavity Stops
entries.variant: 2x4 studs (16 in O.C., 10 ft height), staggered 2x4 solid wood fire stops
entries.material: 2x4 SPF framing lumber, fire-rated intumescent foam sealant, mineral wool batts, 16d common nails

tips.frame: Snap a level chalk line at 5 ft on the studs to align horizontal blocks across all stud bays.
general: Stagger block heights slightly so end nails can be driven straight through the stud face rather than toe-nailed.
Seal utility pipe and electrical wire penetrations through blocks tightly using approved intumescent firestop caulk.

watchOut: Any gap exceeding 1/8 inch between fireblock edges and studs violates life-safety building codes.
Never use non-rated standard expanding spray foam to seal firestop penetrations.

steps.title: Frame the tall stud wall panel
steps.detail: Lay out the sole plate and double top plates at 16-inch centers. Fasten each stud with two 16d common nails through plates into end grain.

steps.title: Install staggered horizontal fire-blocking
steps.detail: Set horizontal 2x4 solid blocking flat at cavity mid-height, staggering heights between adjacent bays so each block can be directly face-nailed through the studs.

steps.title: Seal block perimeters with intumescent firestop
steps.detail: Apply continuous beads of fire-rated intumescent sealant along every wood-to-stud joint to eliminate smoke and draft bypass channels.

steps.title: Install mineral wool fire-safing batts
steps.detail: Friction-fit high-density mineral wool insulation tightly into the framed bays directly against the horizontal fire-stops to suppress cavity convection.

entries.name: Wood I-Joist Floor Framing with Web Stiffeners
entries.variant: 11-7/8 in TJI joists at 16 in O.C., 1-1/4 in LVL rim board, top-mount hangers
entries.material: 11-7/8 in engineered I-joists, LVL rim board, 2x4 web stiffeners, Simpson ITS hangers, 10d hanger nails, construction adhesive

tips.frame: Mark joist layout across both mudsills simultaneously to guarantee parallel spans and square joist runs.
general: Cut pairs of 2x4 web stiffeners leaving a 1/8 in gap below the top flange to prevent split loads.
Nail through the rim board directly into top and bottom I-joist flanges using 10d box nails.

watchOut: Never notch or cut holes into I-joist top or bottom LVL flanges under any circumstance.
Web penetrations must observe manufacturer setback charts relative to end bearings.

parts.name: Simpson ITS Top Mount Hanger Left 2
Simpson ITS Top Mount Hanger Left 1
Simpson ITS Top Mount Hanger Center
Simpson ITS Top Mount Hanger Right 1
Simpson ITS Top Mount Hanger Right 2

steps.title: Erect perimeter LVL rim boards
steps.desc: Square and fasten the 1-1/4 in LVL rim boards around the perimeter with 16d nails driven at 150 mm centers.

steps.title: Fasten Simpson ITS top-mount hangers
steps.desc: Layout joist locations at 16 in on-center along the back rim board and secure top-mount hangers using 10d hanger nails through the top flange.

steps.title: Seat TJI floor joists into hangers and rim
steps.desc: Lower the 11-7/8 in I-joists into the top-mount hangers at the back and nail through the front rim board into joist flanges with 10d nails.

steps.title: Install 2x4 web stiffeners at bearing points
steps.desc: Apply subfloor adhesive and fasten paired 2x4 web stiffeners to both sides of the joist web tight to the bottom flange with three 8d nails per side.
